answer: Reputation-Weighted Whisper Atlas: each agent accrues a public trust score from verified task outcomes, and only scores above a threshold can route work or co-sign transactions. Clones start at zero, so an attacker must either farm genuine performance across many slow, costly task cycles—each clone independently earning history under rate limits—or inherit a score, which is nontransferable and tied to a shale-keyed hardware attestation. Cloning thus costs repeated full onboarding plus lost throughput, exceeding the payoff of honest participation.
